page.title: How the 14-day refund window is counted
page.markdown:
# How the 14-day refund window is counted

*Community guide, last updated March 2026*

A lot of people in the forums have asked how Harbor Notes counts the 14-day refund window. Here's a summary of how it works, based on answers from support threads.

## Business days, not calendar days

The window is **14 business days** (Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays). Weekends don't count. A payment made on a Saturday starts counting on the following Monday.

**Example:** paid Saturday 28 February → day 1 is Monday 2 March → day 14 is Thursday 19 March.

## The first contact date is what counts

If you asked for a refund through any channel (in-app chat, email or the support form) inside the window, your request counts as made on that date. This holds even if the formal ticket was opened later because the chat didn't get a follow-up. Mention the date of your first contact in your ticket.

## Other things to know

- Duplicate charges are always refunded, whatever the date.
- You can get one refund on request in any 12 months.
- Refunds over $200 are reviewed by staff before they're issued.

## Tips for a smooth request

1. Include your invoice number (e.g. INV-000123).
2. Say when you first contacted support.
3. Briefly explain the reason. It helps the product team.

*Have a correction? Edit this page or post in the Community forum.*

page.title: What counts as a duplicate charge?
page.markdown:
# What counts as a duplicate charge?

*Community guide, last updated March 2026*

Harbor Notes refunds duplicate charges whatever the date. People often ask what "duplicate" covers, so here's a summary pulled from support threads.

## Same charge twice

The obvious case: the same card is charged twice for the same invoice, for example after a checkout that timed out and was retried.

## Same plan bought through two stores

This is the most common case people miss. If you already subscribe to Pro through the **iOS App Store** or **Google Play**, the web app can't always see that subscription. It may show an "upgrade" prompt, and clicking it creates a second web subscription. You then pay twice for the same plan over the same period.

Support treats the web charge as a **duplicate charge**, so the usual 14-day window doesn't apply. Keep your store subscription. The web invoice is the one that gets refunded.

## What is *not* a duplicate

- Upgrading from one plan to another (that's a proration).
- Two different accounts each with their own plan.
- Renewals for different billing periods.

## Tips

1. Give the invoice number of the web charge (e.g. INV-000123).
2. Say which store you subscribe through and roughly when it renews.
3. Don't cancel the store subscription first, or you may lose Pro access while support looks at it.

*Have a correction? Edit this page or post in the Community forum.*
